The boy who embraces the challenge picks up the ball and tries again anyway after being hit on the elbow.

(A) Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard.

(B) The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team.

(C) He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [원문] (B) learns → regional team / (A) national championship → finals / (C) match point → triumph [해석] 지역팀(B) → 전국 대회(A) → 결승 승리(C)

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task.

questions.passage: The answer lies in resilience—the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience.

det.ref: [원문] (A) the ability to adapt to challenging experiences / (B) you must experience difficulties [해석] (A) 적응하는 능력 / (B) 어려움을 경험해야 함.
det.correct:

(B) experience: experience difficulties(어려움을 경험하다) ✅
동명사 형태(adapting/experiencing)도 허용.
det.tip: 🔑 adapt(v.) = 적응하다 ≈ adjust, accommodate ↔ resist. adapt to + 명사. experience(v.)=경험하다; (n.)=경험. 면역 비유: germs→immunity = difficulties→resilience.

questions.passage: Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going.
